## Purpose

A result struct in `pipeline/`/`review/qa_run/` is the pure, side-effect-free outcome of one decision function — separate from the code that acts on it (writes a metric, prints JSON, exits with a code). `close_gates.rs` uses this shape for its multi-gate decision engine, `status.rs` and `pipeline_summary.rs` build a result before rendering. Keeping the result pure means the decision logic (e.g. which gate denied, what the header/status word is) is unit-testable without touching disk or the event log.

## Convention

Folder: apps/rt/src/commands/pipeline/**, apps/rt/src/commands/review/qa_run/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 5

Fields are named after what was DECIDED, not how — `Header { status, name, lang }` in `pipeline_summary.rs`, not raw markdown offsets. Construction is via a free function taking the raw inputs (`parse_header(text: &str) -> Header`), often followed by an `apply_*_override` step that layers a more-authoritative source (`meta.json`) on top of the legacy one (the markdown header) — fields the override does not declare keep the legacy value.

## How to apply

Define the result as a small `struct` (private/`pub(crate)` unless a sibling command needs it), built by a pure function that takes already-read text/data, never a `Path`. Apply any override/cascade logic as a separate function taking ownership of the base result and returning the adjusted one (`apply_meta_override(mut header: Header, ...) -> Header`), so each layer of precedence is independently testable.

## Examples

Ref: apps/rt/src/commands/pipeline/pipeline_summary.rs
Ref: apps/rt/src/commands/pipeline/close_gates.rs

```rust
/// Lifecycle status word + spec name + language for the summary header line.
/// `pub(crate)` so `close-pipeline` can drive [`build_for_dir`] in-process.
pub(crate) struct Header {
    status: String,
    name: String,
    lang: String,
}
```
